project.name: The Social Game
project.description: Social gaming platform with real-time mechanics, event sourcing, and AI integration

keyDirectories.app/Events/: Event sourcing events for state changes
keyDirectories.mcp/: Model Context Protocol server for AI integration
keyDirectories.docs/: Project documentation including AI development guide

coreModels.Game: Game instances with settings and state
coreModels.GamePlayer: Many-to-many relationship between users and games

gameFlow: Game creation with templates and modes

mcpIntegration.purpose: Provides AI assistants structured access to game data

developmentCommands.cd mcp && npm run dev: Start MCP server in development mode

testingSetup.pattern: Test everything through Livewire to prove frontend integration
testingSetup.helpers: Use TestCase methods: mockGameTemplate(), createGame(), createPlayer()

deploymentConsiderations.queues: Requires queue workers for background processing
deploymentConsiderations.caching: Redis recommended for sessions and cache

conventionsAndPatterns.stateChanges: All state changes must go through Events
conventionsAndPatterns.database: Use migrations for schema changes, UUIDs for primary keys
conventionsAndPatterns.validation: Form Requests and custom Rules classes

whenMakingChanges: Always consider the gaming domain and social aspects
CRITICAL: Use ONLY Verbs events for database changes - NEVER direct model updates
CRITICAL: Use only Livewire + Alpine.js - no other frontend frameworks
CRITICAL: Keep GameDashboard/PlayerView/TeamView completely generic and game-agnostic
CRITICAL: Write comprehensive Livewire integration tests for all features
Follow the architectural patterns in docs/architectural-patterns.md
Use GameDashboard + HandlesClassActions pattern for UI interactions
Challenge/Modifier classes should extend Base classes and follow established patterns
Frontend components should be generated via frontendComponent() methods
Update documentation when adding major features
aiDevelopmentNotes.mcpAwareness: The MCP server in mcp/ directory provides AI assistants with database access and game information. Reference mcp/README.md for available tools and resources.

corePatterns.gameInteractions: GameDashboard (Livewire) + HandlesClassActions trait + Challenge/Modifier classes + form.blade.php component
corePatterns.stateChanges: All via Verbs events with validate() -> apply() -> handle() pattern
corePatterns.uiGeneration: Classes generate frontendComponent() arrays, rendered by form.blade.php
corePatterns.actionHandling: callClassAction() validates, calls handler method, fires events, commits via Verbs::commit()
corePatterns.lifecycle: mount() -> initializeProperties() -> user interaction -> callClassAction() -> event -> refresh

keyInsights: This is an event-sourced system - all important state changes are events
NEVER update database directly - only through Verbs events or state becomes inconsistent
GameDashboard is a 'superhighway' - completely agnostic to game content
New game modes should work automatically without frontend changes
All features must be tested through Livewire to prove frontend integration
Livewire + Alpine.js ONLY - no React/Vue/other frontend frameworks
Real-time features are crucial - many actions need WebSocket updates
Game fairness and preventing cheating should be considered
Challenge and Modifier classes define both backend logic AND frontend UI
HandlesClassActions trait bridges Livewire frontend with class-based backend
Payment integration exists for premium features
